newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends higher ahead of fresh data.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends higher ahead of fresh data.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled firmer ahead of the first notice day for the May contract, the weekly export and sales report, and monthly consumption data.
Analysts said expectations for few deliveries and steadiness in sales and consumption in Thursday's numbers may have provided support to an otherwise weak market.
Activity remained focused on the spread amid brisk volume estimated at 25,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's official 17,925 lots.
"Our job today is to liquidate May," Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said.
Next week, the market could see a short-covering rally that could carry prices sharply higher, she said.
Open interest in May stood at 7,896 lots, down 4,113 lots as of Monday's close.
Support was pegged at 72.00 cents in July, below the life-of-contract low of 72.05 cents.
July finished 0.55 cent per lb firmer at 73.45 cents, having ranged from 73.50 to 72.76 cents per lb. Spot May closed 0.29 cent higher at 71.37 cents.
